key_insight: First-principles electronic-structure, phonon, and loss-function calculations can predict electron-hole-pair creation energy in semiconductors and dielectrics, with the balance between phonon emission and ionization setting the final value.
engineering_relevance: These creation energies help model radiation response, carrier thermalization, and breakdown-related behavior in device materials such as Si, SiC, AlN, and SiO2.
method: TDDFT plus full-band Monte Carlo for energy-loss and thermalization; GW/BSE refinement for Si
evidence_signal: Predicted pair-creation energies were ~12.2 eV (AlN), 6.5 eV (3C-SiC), 7.3 eV (4H-SiC), 3.10 eV (Si), and 16.7 eV (SiO2), with GW/BSE improving Si to ~3.50 eV/pair and reducing the discrepancy to experiment.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on high-fidelity quasiparticle and dielectric calculations, and the results can be sensitive to the low-energy loss function and the assumed competition between phonon scattering and ionization.
paper_title: First-Principles Calculations of the Electron-Hole-Pair Creation Energy in Semiconductors and Dielectrics
